approvalRequirements: Be an Iowa business or industry proposing a qualifying energy-efficiency equipment replacement project; manufacturers receive preference.
Demonstrate quantifiable efficiency gains and provide the project scope, costs, and requested financing amount to IADG.
Satisfy IADG's project and financing review and remain within the current loan-size and program-fund limits.
Execute the approved loan documents before project funding is released.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The Energy Bank is an ongoing low-interest revolving loan fund, but financing is not automatic. The project must demonstrate measurable efficiency gains and pass IADG's project and financing review while funds are available.
reviews.evidenceText: IADG currently describes a $2 million revolving fund offering 1% loans of $50,000 to $300,000 for Iowa business and industry efficiency projects, with preference for manufacturers and quantifiable savings required.

approvalRequirements: Wait for Idaho to resume the paused NEVI program and publish a direct application or solicitation.
Propose an eligible charging site on a designated Alternative Fuel Corridor unless federal corridor build-out certification permits broader locations.
Design a NEVI-compliant DC fast-charging station, including at least four CCS ports capable of 150 kW each and at least 600 kW total station output.
Submit the required site, technical, financial, match, ownership, operating, maintenance, and reporting information.
Pass state and federal review and execute an award agreement before reimbursable work proceeds.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Idaho's official NEVI page states that the program is paused for federal agency review and does not provide an open direct application. A future award would also require a compliant corridor project and state selection.
reviews.evidenceText: Idaho currently identifies NEVI as paused while the state develops a direct-application program and lists corridor and high-power DC fast-charging requirements for funded stations.

approvalRequirements: Own an eligible commercial property in an Idaho jurisdiction that has established an active C-PACE program, such as Boise.
Use the financing for a permanent qualified improvement accepted by the local program, with battery storage qualifying only if approved as an eligible resiliency measure.
Secure a willing private capital provider and satisfy its underwriting, project-cost, property, and repayment requirements.
Submit the local program application and required property, project, ownership, tax, title, and financing documentation.
Obtain any required mortgage-holder consent and execute the voluntary assessment and lien documents before closing.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Idaho law permits local C-PACE programs, and Boise has an active application pathway, but access depends on local adoption, project qualification, private-capital underwriting, lien consent, and final program approval.
reviews.evidenceText: Boise's current C-PACE program allows private financing for qualifying commercial energy-efficiency, renewable-energy, water-conservation, and resiliency improvements through a voluntary property assessment and recorded lien.

approvalRequirements: Receive commercial or industrial electric service from Idaho Falls Power.
Schedule an Idaho Falls Power building audit before installing the energy-saving measure to be financed.
Submit a qualifying conservation project and loan request within the applicable project-cost and loan limits.
Complete the approved installation and permit Idaho Falls Power to conduct final verification before funds are issued.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The only mapped retrofit is an energy audit, but the official program describes the audit as a prerequisite for financing installed efficiency measures rather than as a separately financed conservation project. A loan for the audit itself is therefore unlikely under the documented scope.
reviews.evidenceText: Idaho Falls Power currently requires a pre-installation building audit and offers zero-interest loans for qualifying installed efficiency measures, not a stated standalone loan for the audit service.

approvalRequirements: Receive commercial or industrial electric service from Idaho Falls Power.
Have Idaho Falls Power determine preliminary project qualification and complete the required audit or pre-inspection before equipment purchase and installation.
Install qualifying lighting, HVAC, or other approved efficiency equipment consistent with the reviewed project scope.
Provide completion information and allow Idaho Falls Power to perform a final inspection before payment.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: This is a rule-based utility incentive rather than a ranked grant competition. A qualifying Idaho Falls Power customer that completes the required advance audit and passes final installation verification is likely to receive the published rebate.
reviews.evidenceText: Idaho Falls Power currently requires service eligibility and a pre-installation audit, then issues commercial efficiency rebates after a final inspection verifies the qualifying installation.

approvalRequirements: Receive residential electric service from Idaho Falls Power and meet the measure-specific home and heating eligibility rules.
Complete the required free energy consultation before purchasing or installing the proposed weatherization measure.
Have at least one year of satisfactory City utility payment history, no current delinquency, and owner authorization when the applicant is not the building owner.
Submit contractor bids or the proposed work for Idaho Falls Power review and obtain a final financing determination and Notice to Proceed before work starts.
Complete the approved work and pass the final inspection before the allowable loan amount is paid.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The zero-interest loan is available through a defined process, but approval depends on payment history, property and measure eligibility, bid and financing review, advance authorization, and final inspection rather than solely on completing insulation or weatherization work.
reviews.evidenceText: Idaho Falls Power currently requires an advance home consultation, good utility payment history, bid and financing approval, a Notice to Proceed, and final inspection for residential weatherization loans.

approvalRequirements: Receive residential electric service from Idaho Falls Power and satisfy the measure-specific home, existing-equipment, and heating-fuel requirements.
Complete an Idaho Falls Power energy consultation before purchase or installation when the selected measure requires one.
Use qualifying equipment and an eligible installation method or contractor and submit the applicable application and supporting equipment information.
Allow final inspection or other verification before the rebate is issued.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Idaho Falls Power publishes measure-specific residential rebates and uses administrative qualification and verification rather than competitive ranking. A compliant customer submission is likely to be paid after any required consultation and inspection.
reviews.evidenceText: Current Idaho Falls Power pages list residential rebates for qualifying heat pumps, geothermal systems, insulation, windows, and related measures, with consultation, equipment, application, and verification requirements varying by measure.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Idaho Power commercial or industrial customer with a qualifying electrical energy-saving project not already covered by a prescriptive retrofit or new-construction measure.
Prepare the project scope, cost estimate, energy-savings calculations, and requested incentive information.
Submit the preapproval portion of the application and receive written Idaho Power approval before proceeding.
Obtain approval for material scope changes and permit any requested pre- or post-installation measurement and verification.
After completion, submit the payment application with itemized material and labor invoices and required final documentation.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Custom incentives require project-specific cost-effectiveness, savings calculations, written advance approval, and measurement and verification. Approval is therefore possible but not automatic even for a technically plausible project.
reviews.evidenceText: Idaho Power currently requires a custom-project application with calculations and cost data, written preapproval before work, final invoices, and measurement and verification before issuing an incentive.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Idaho Power business customer and install a currently listed retrofit measure that meets the applicable technical specifications.
Obtain written preapproval before starting work whenever the measure or estimated incentive triggers advance approval under the current program rules.
Complete the project as approved and retain product specifications, itemized material and labor invoices, and proof of payment.
Submit the payment application within the applicable post-completion deadline and allow an onsite inspection if selected.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The retrofit offering is generally prescriptive and administrative rather than competitively scored. A qualifying project that obtains any required advance approval and submits complete timely documentation is likely to receive the calculated incentive, subject to current terms and funds.
reviews.evidenceText: Idaho Power currently offers business retrofit incentives through measure-specific Idaho pathways, with advance approval for designated projects and final applications supported by invoices, specifications, and possible inspection.

approvalRequirements: Be an Idaho Power commercial or industrial customer undertaking eligible new construction, an addition, an expansion, or a major renovation.
Submit a preliminary application before project completion and identify any custom measures requiring separate custom-project review.
Install qualifying measures that exceed applicable code requirements and meet the current equipment or design specifications.

Submit the signed final application within 90 days after completion with product data, proof of performance, paid invoices, and measure-specific documentation such as COMcheck or a control-strategy summary.
Permit an onsite inspection before payment if the project is selected for verification.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The program provides defined incentives for qualifying above-code projects and is not a ranked solicitation. A timely, properly documented project is likely to be paid after technical review and any selected inspection.
reviews.evidenceText: Idaho Power currently requires a preliminary application before completion, a final application within 90 days, above-code performance, supporting specifications and invoices, and possible onsite inspection.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Idaho Power residential customer or property owner in Oregon and select a measure currently offered for the property and installation type.
Meet all measure-specific home, existing-equipment, efficiency, contractor, and installation requirements.
Complete a pre-project Oregon energy audit or other advance program step when required for the selected weatherization or rebate pathway.
Submit the applicable claim form, contractor or customer worksheet, paid invoice, equipment certification, and other required documentation by the stated deadline.
Allow inspection or verification when requested.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Idaho Power's residential incentives use published, measure-specific eligibility and documentation rules rather than competitive ranking. A currently covered Oregon measure is likely to receive the listed incentive after any required audit and claim review.
reviews.evidenceText: Idaho Power currently lists residential heating, cooling, weatherization, and related offers, with Oregon pathways requiring measure-specific qualifications, documentation, and an advance audit where applicable.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Idaho Power residential customer or property owner in Idaho and choose a currently offered qualifying measure.
Meet the selected measure's home, existing-equipment, efficiency, sizing, and installation requirements.
Use a participating contractor before purchase or installation whenever the measure-specific pathway requires one.
Submit the applicable application or contractor worksheet, paid invoice, product data, and required certifications.
Permit inspection or other program verification if requested.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The Idaho residential offering is a formulaic rebate program with measure-specific conditions. Once the required contractor, equipment, installation, and documentation rules are satisfied, payment is likely after administrative review.
reviews.evidenceText: Idaho Power currently offers residential heating and cooling incentives through measure-specific pages that require qualifying equipment, installation conditions, applications, invoices, and program review.

approvalRequirements: Be a commercial customer located in Imperial Irrigation District's electric service area.
Propose a refrigeration or other efficiency measure that exceeds applicable Title 24 requirements or an IID-approved baseline.
Apply for a preliminary energy analysis before committing to the project and provide the necessary savings calculations, scope, and cost information.
Submit the current application, rebate agreement, installation report, and supporting technical and financial documentation.
Complete the approved project and pass IID's final review or verification while program funds remain available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: IID's custom program requires a project-specific energy analysis and technical approval, and incentives are limited and first-come, first-served. A qualifying refrigeration project can be funded, but award is not automatic.
reviews.evidenceText: IID's 2026 Custom Energy Solutions Program serves commercial customers, requires above-baseline savings and a preliminary energy analysis, and offers limited first-come incentives supported by current application and completion forms.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible IID residential electric customer at the installation address.
Purchase and install a currently qualifying product during the applicable 2026 program period and meet all measure-specific efficiency and installation rules.
Use an IID participating contractor when required for the selected HVAC, mini-split, or insulation measure.
Submit the online application by December 31, 2026 with an invoice or receipt showing brand, model, proof of purchase, and all measure-specific documentation.
Allow IID to verify the installation or supporting information if requested.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: IID publishes current measure-specific rebate amounts and administrative claim requirements. A qualifying 2026 purchase with complete documentation is likely to receive the rebate after review, subject to program terms and funds.
reviews.evidenceText: IID's current residential page requires qualifying products to be purchased and installed in 2026, applications by December 31, and invoices showing product and payment details plus measure-specific evidence.

approvalRequirements: Submit a Round 4 location prequalification package by the July 20, 2026 deadline.
Propose an Illinois charging location and project that complies with current federal NEVI rules and the requirements stated by IDOT for the round.

Provide the required environmental determination form, project-location and project-area maps, site photographs, and any subsequently requested technical, financial, ownership, utility, and operating information.
Demonstrate the ability to provide the required nonfederal share and to build, operate, maintain, and report on the charging infrastructure.
Pass IDOT's competitive review and execute the grant or reimbursement agreement before award-funded work.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Illinois Round 4 is currently open with approximately $30 million available, but applications must meet federal requirements and compete for IDOT selection. Eligibility and a complete submission do not assure an award.
reviews.evidenceText: IDOT currently has Round 4 open through July 20, 2026 for organizations and businesses to prequalify Illinois locations, with federal compliance and specified environmental and site documents required.

approvalRequirements: No current application can be submitted because the Illinois Clean Energy Community Foundation ceased operations effective December 2024.

A historical applicant would have needed to meet the applicable grant-program criteria, submit an application, receive Foundation selection and approval, and execute the grant requirements before funding.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The Foundation states that it ceased operations in December 2024 and made its final grant. New solar-water-heating, biomass, or biogas awards from this named program are therefore extraordinarily unlikely.
reviews.evidenceText: The Foundation's official site states that operations ceased effective December 2024 and that a final grant was made as the organization ended its work.

approvalRequirements: Be a qualifying retail customer of an IMEA member municipal electric system with an eligible Illinois efficiency project.
Confirm local funding availability and submit a complete current preapplication before beginning the project.
Obtain IMEA review, member-municipality approval, any required preinspection, and a written Notice to Proceed before work starts.
Comply with any additional municipal caps, limits, rules, and the approved project scope.
Submit the final application, paid itemized invoices, product information, and other required documents within 45 days after completion and allow site verification.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: All projects need preapproval, funds can be exhausted quickly, and the member municipality may offer any amount from zero up to the qualified maximum and may impose additional rules. An award is possible but discretionary and budget-dependent.
reviews.evidenceText: IMEA currently requires preapproval and a Notice to Proceed for every project; the member municipality decides the offered amount, funds may go quickly, and final invoices and documentation are due within 45 days.

approvalRequirements: Own or develop an eligible privately owned commercial, industrial, nonresidential agricultural, multifamily, or nonprofit property in an Illinois PACE area.
Use financing for a permanent eligible improvement, with battery storage accepted only if it qualifies as an energy, renewable-energy, or resiliency improvement under the program.
Secure an approved private capital provider and satisfy its underwriting, project-cost, property-value, and repayment conditions.
Submit the current IFA PACE application and required ownership, project, legal, tax, title, and financing documentation.
Obtain all required local assessment-contract approvals and execute the financing, assessment, lien, and bond or note documents.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The IFA PACE program provides an active statewide framework in participating PACE areas, but financing depends on property and project eligibility, private-capital underwriting, local approval, and execution of assessment and financing documents.
reviews.evidenceText: The Illinois Finance Authority currently supports C-PACE projects in listed counties and municipalities for eligible permanent efficiency, renewable-energy, resiliency, water, and EV-charging improvements financed by private capital.

approvalRequirements: Fit an active Illinois Solar for All subprogram, including income-eligible residential solar, community solar, or qualifying nonprofit and public-facility solar.
Develop and submit the project through an Illinois Solar for All Approved Vendor that is also approved through Illinois Shines.
Meet participant eligibility, site suitability, technical, consumer-protection, guaranteed-savings, disclosure, contract, job-training, and community-engagement requirements that apply.
Submit the Part I project application during the applicable 2026-2027 project window and cure any deficiencies within program deadlines.
Pass project eligibility review and, if requests exceed the subprogram budget, the Project Selection Protocol before REC contract approval and later energization obligations.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The 2026-2027 program is active, but projects must be submitted by an Approved Vendor, satisfy extensive eligibility and consumer-protection rules, and may be ranked under the Project Selection Protocol when a subprogram is oversubscribed.
reviews.evidenceText: Illinois Solar for All currently operates through vetted Approved Vendors, requires guaranteed participant savings and technical and consumer protections, and uses timed project windows with competitive selection if requests exceed a subprogram budget.

approvalRequirements: Make the upgrade to an Idaho residence that is the taxpayer's primary residence and that existed, was under construction, or had an outstanding legal building permit on or before January 1, 2002.
Install an eligible building-envelope or duct-system improvement that meets or exceeds the Idaho IECC minimum applicable for the tax year.
Limit the claim to qualifying costs for measures such as added insulation, eligible windows, weather stripping or caulking, or mechanically fastened and mastic-sealed duct sealing and insulation.
Report the deduction on the current Idaho individual return and Form 39R and retain invoices, proof of payment, installation details, and efficiency documentation.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: This is a statutory income-tax deduction rather than a competitively awarded program. A taxpayer who satisfies the residence, measure, code, cost, and filing requirements should ordinarily receive the deduction, subject to normal return processing and audit authority.
reviews.evidenceText: Current Idaho instructions describe a deduction for qualifying envelope and duct upgrades to an eligible pre-2002 primary residence, with IECC compliance, Form 39R reporting, and supporting records required.

approvalRequirements: Purchase equipment or an appliance that qualifies under the current Virginia energy-efficient-product deduction rules.
Pay Virginia retail sales or use tax on the qualifying purchase and retain the receipt showing the item and tax paid.
Calculate the deduction as 20% of the qualifying sales tax, subject to the annual cap of $500 for an individual return or $1,000 for a joint return.
Report the deduction on the current Virginia Schedule ADJ using the applicable deduction code and retain records for possible review.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The benefit is a statutory tax deduction rather than a limited competitive award. When the purchased product is currently qualifying and the sales-tax amount, cap, and filing rules are correctly documented, allowance is ordinarily expected subject to tax review.
reviews.evidenceText: Virginia currently allows a deduction equal to 20% of sales tax paid on certain energy-efficient equipment or appliances, capped at $500 per individual return or $1,000 for a joint return.

approvalRequirements: Be an Independence Power and Light business or industrial customer with a qualifying efficiency project.
Use the prescriptive application for qualifying air-conditioning work or the custom application for LED lighting, lighting controls, or other projects outside the prescriptive categories.
For a custom project, demonstrate a simple payback between two and ten years and provide project scope, cost, equipment, and savings documentation.
Obtain any required advance approval under the current program rules before committing to the work.
Submit completion and cost documentation and comply with the maximum incentive of $20,000 or 30% of project cost, whichever is less.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: HVAC projects may use a prescriptive route, but the mapped lighting and control measures generally require a custom application, technical payback review, and program approval. The incentive is therefore possible rather than automatic.
reviews.evidenceText: Independence Power and Light currently offers prescriptive air-conditioning rebates and custom rebates requiring a two-to-ten-year simple payback, with a $20,000 or 30%-of-cost annual cap.

approvalRequirements: Construct a new home served by Independence Power and Light and have it evaluated by an independent Home Energy Rating System rater.
Complete the required onsite inspections and performance testing, including blower-door and duct testing as applicable.
Achieve ENERGY STAR certification and install any claimed HVAC or water-heating equipment at the required efficiency level.
Submit the IPL-provided incentive application, HERS rating and certification records, equipment information, and supporting cost documentation.
Do not claim overlapping standard IPL residential equipment rebates for measures paid through the new-homes program.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The new-homes rebate follows published certification and equipment criteria rather than competitive ranking. A builder whose home achieves ENERGY STAR status and submits the required IPL documentation is likely to receive the stated reimbursement and equipment incentive.
reviews.evidenceText: IPL currently requires an independent HERS rating, onsite testing, ENERGY STAR certification, and program applications, and offers reimbursement for rating costs plus qualifying HVAC or water-heating incentives.

approvalRequirements: Be an Independence Power and Light residential customer at the installation address.
Purchase and install a qualifying air conditioner or heat pump that meets the current minimum efficiency standards.
Complete the applicable rebate application and submit it with a detailed receipt and required equipment information.
Permit a site inspection when IPL determines that verification is necessary.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: IPL's residential equipment rebates are administrative and use published efficiency requirements. A complete claim for qualifying equipment is likely to be approved after document review and any requested inspection.
reviews.evidenceText: IPL currently directs residential customers to submit an equipment-specific application and detailed receipt, verifies minimum efficiency, may require a site inspection, and pays approved rebates as account credits.

approvalRequirements: For a previously announced contingent award, satisfy INDOT's contracting, site-control, technical, cost-share, permitting, construction, operation, maintenance, and reporting conditions.
For a new project, wait for INDOT to announce a future application phase and submit a responsive competitive proposal by the stated deadline.
Use an eligible Indiana corridor or other location permitted under the applicable phase and meet current federal NEVI charging and accessibility standards.
Provide the required nonfederal match and all site, utility, environmental, financial, ownership, and operating documentation.
Receive INDOT selection and execute the funding agreement before relying on reimbursement.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: INDOT has resumed contracting only for contingent awards announced in 2024, while future application phases have not yet been announced. A new applicant therefore has no current open award path and would later face competitive selection.
reviews.evidenceText: Indiana currently reports resumed contracting for 2024 contingent NEVI awards and states that information about future phases will be released later; no new application round is posted.
